title: A class of site coverings admits a set of representatives with prescribed coverings
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category whose objects and arrows form sets. Let $\operatorname{Cov}$ be a possibly proper class of set-indexed families of arrows with a common target, satisfying the three covering axioms of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), without the requirement that the collection of families be a set: every singleton isomorphism is in $\operatorname{Cov}$; composites of a family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ with families in $\operatorname{Cov}$ on each of its domains are in $\operatorname{Cov}$; and for any family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ and any arrow to its target all the required fibre products exist and the pulled-back family is in $\operatorname{Cov}$. For every set $\operatorname{Cov}_0\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ there is a set $\operatorname{Cov}'$ with $\operatorname{Cov}_0\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}'\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ satisfying the same three axioms, such that every family in $\operatorname{Cov}$ is combinatorially equivalent to a family in $\operatorname{Cov}'$. Here combinatorially equivalent means that the two families have the same target and the same set of arrows, ignoring repetitions.

source.place: Tag 000X (sets-lemma-coverings-site), clauses (1)-(3); hypotheses and combinatorial equivalence in Section 000W

proof.text: Put $A=\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C)$ and $O=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$. The pairs $(U,T)$ with $U\in O$ and $T\subseteq\{a\in A:\operatorname{target}(a)=U\}$ form a set. By Separation take the subset $P$ of pairs that occur as the target and arrow support of a family in $\operatorname{Cov}$. For each $p\in P$ there is a set-coded witnessing family; the ZFC Collection axiom gives a set of such witnesses, and Choice selects one for each $p$. Thus obtain a set $R\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ representing every target/support pair. Recording the target separately is necessary for empty families. Equal supports at equal targets give the required equivalence (one chooses an occurrence of each arrow in each family); no reindexing or removal of repetitions is asserted to preserve membership in the original class.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), first paragraph; target included to cover empty supports; Collection replaces the equivalent least-rank witness construction

proof.text: Let $B_0$ be the union of $R$, $\operatorname{Cov}_0$, and the standard singleton families of all isomorphisms. It is a set contained in $\operatorname{Cov}$. Choose an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ bounding $|A|$, $|O|$ and every index cardinal of a family in $B_0$ (take the supremum of this set of cardinals and $\aleph_0$). For a set $K$ of cardinality $\kappa$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality] gives $|\operatorname{List}(K)|\leq\kappa$. The map $(x,y)\mapsto[x,y]$ is injective, so $|K\times K|\leq\kappa$. Consequently if $|I|\leq\kappa$ and all $|J_i|\leq\kappa$, choose injections into $K$ to inject $\coprod_i J_i$ into $K\times K$, giving cardinality at most $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), second paragraph, infinite cardinal arithmetic; Tag 000D (section-cardinals)

proof.text: Let $\theta$ be the least ordinal of cardinality greater than $\kappa$. It is nonzero and a limit: adjoining one element to an infinite set of size at most $\kappa$ preserves that bound (encode it in $K\times K$), so it cannot be a successor. Every $\gamma<\theta$ has size at most $\kappa$. If a cofinal subset $T\subseteq\theta$ had size at most $\kappa$, the equality $\theta=\bigcup_{t\in T}t$ and the disjoint-union estimate in step 2 would imply $|\theta|\leq\kappa$, a contradiction. Thus $\operatorname{cf}(\theta)>\kappa$. Cofinality means the least size of a cofinal subset, where cofinal means every earlier ordinal is at most some member.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] on the set of stages $\gamma\leq\theta$ to define increasing sets $B_\gamma$. Start with the $B_0$ of step 2. At a successor add to $B_\gamma$ every composite of an outer family in $B_\gamma$ and a choice of a family in $B_\gamma$ on each of its domains, and, for each family in $B_\gamma$ and arrow of $A$, one chosen pullback family supplied by the site axiom (Choice selects one such fibre-product presentation for each pair). At a nonzero limit take the union of the earlier stages. These successor additions form sets: for each outer index set $I$, all choices of inner families lie in the set of maps $I\to B_\gamma$; all selected base-change data are indexed by $B_\gamma\times A$, with the pullback objects and projections in the fixed sets $O,A$. Induction proves $B_\gamma\subseteq\operatorname{Cov}$ by the given axioms and proves every family has index cardinal at most $\kappa$ by step 2; pullbacks retain the index set and composites have index set $\coprod_iJ_i$.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), transfinite closure construction; direct sets of families in place of rank cutoffs

proof.text: Set $\operatorname{Cov}\prime=B_\theta=\bigcup_{\gamma<\theta}B_\gamma$, a set. It contains $\operatorname{Cov}_0$ and all singleton isomorphisms and is contained in $\operatorname{Cov}$. If a family belongs to it, it belongs to some $B_\gamma$ with $\gamma<\theta$; the selected pullback family supplied by the original class axiom belongs to $B_{\gamma+1}\subseteq B_\theta$, since $\theta$ is a limit. The existence of the fibre products and the covering property for this selected choice are exactly the original class axiom. This proves the identity and base-change axioms.

For the composition axiom take an outer family $\mathcal U\in B_\theta$, indexed by $I$, and inner families $\mathcal W_i\in B_\theta$. Choose $\gamma_0<\theta$ and $\gamma_i<\theta$ with $\mathcal U\in B_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathcal W_i\in B_{\gamma_i}$. Since $|I|\leq\kappa<\operatorname{cf}(\theta)$, [lem-weil-pbc-cofinality-small-family-bound] gives $\sup_i\gamma_i<\theta$. Put $\gamma=\max(\gamma_0,\sup_i\gamma_i)<\theta$. Monotonicity places the outer and every inner family in $B_\gamma$, so their composite lies in $B_{\gamma+1}\subseteq B_\theta$. If $I$ is empty its supremum is $0$, and the same argument works. Finally $R\subseteq B_0\subseteq B_\theta$ ensures every original family has an equivalent representative, proving the last clause.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), final paragraph and condition (3); repair beta<beta_1 to beta<beta_2 and include the outer stage
